accepted.s: The first session of the Indian National Congress was shifted from Poona to Bombay because of
accepted.x: The proposed session at Poona was shifted to Bombay because of a cholera outbreak.
accepted.tq: Test the specific cause of a venue change rather than merely recalling the final venue.
accepted.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: At which of the following places was the first session of the Indian National Congress held?
accepted.x: The inaugural session met at the Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College in Bombay.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact institutional venue from the city of the session.
accepted.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who served as the General Secretary of the Indian National Congress at its foundation?
accepted.x: A.O. Hume became the General Secretary of the Indian National Congress at its foundation.
accepted.tq: Ask who performed the organisational role instead of who presided over the session.
accepted.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the first session of the Indian National Congress:
1. It was attended by 72 delegates.
2. W.C. Bonnerjee presided over it.
3. A.O. Hume served as its General Secretary.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the first session had 72 delegates, was presided over by W.C. Bonnerjee, and had A.O. Hume as General Secretary.
accepted.tq: Check all three linked facts about the inaugural session before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the composition of the delegates to the first session of the Indian National Congress?
o: 54 Hindus and 2 Muslims, besides Jains and Parsis
36 Hindus and 36 Muslims, besides Jains and Parsis
54 Muslims and 2 Hindus, besides Sikhs and Christians
72 Hindus, with no delegates from other communities
accepted.x: The 72 delegates included 54 Hindus and 2 Muslims, along with Jains and Parsis.
accepted.tq: Test composition figures through a precise membership comparison.
accepted.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The delegates to the first session of the Indian National Congress were drawn mainly from which occupational groups?
accepted.x: Most delegates were lawyers, journalists and teachers.
accepted.tq: Identify the social-professional base of the early Congress from closely related occupational groups.
accepted.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the demands of the first session of the Indian National Congress?
o: Simultaneous ICS examinations in England and India
Immediate establishment of complete provincial autonomy
Opposition to the annexation of Upper Burma
Election in place of nomination for councils
accepted.x: The first session demanded simultaneous ICS examinations, elected councils, opposition to the annexation of Upper Burma and reduction of military expenditure. Immediate complete provincial autonomy was not listed among its four demands.
accepted.tq: Find the one demand that falls outside the specific four-point programme.
accepted.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following combinations correctly represents two demands of the first session of the Indian National Congress?
1. Simultaneous ICS examinations in England and India
2. Reduction in military expenditure
3. Annexation of Upper Burma
4. Nomination instead of election to councils
accepted.x: The session demanded simultaneous ICS examinations and cuts in military expenditure. It opposed the annexation of Upper Burma and sought election instead of nomination to councils.
accepted.tq: Reverse the wording of two demands to detect the false alternatives.
accepted.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Private meeting of 17 persons after the Theosophical Convention at Madras
B. First session of the Indian National Congress
C. Second session of the Indian National Congress
D. Formation of Hume's Indian National Union
accepted.x: The private meeting followed the December 1884 Theosophical Convention, Hume's Indian National Union preceded the Congress, the first session was held in 1885, and the second in 1886.
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence around the 1884 origin and the 1885–1886 Congress sessions.
accepted.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The origin of the Indian National Congress is associated with a private meeting of how many persons after the Theosophical Convention at Madras in December 1884?
accepted.x: A private meeting of 17 persons after the Theosophical Convention at Madras is associated with the early origin of the Congress.
accepted.tq: Use the exact small-number detail rather than confusing it with delegate figures.
accepted.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which organisation was associated with A.O. Hume before the establishment of the Indian National Congress?
accepted.x: A.O. Hume's Indian National Union is identified as one of the organisational origins of the Congress.
accepted.tq: Distinguish Hume's organisation from other pre-Congress political bodies.
accepted.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The credit for giving the organisation the name “Indian National Congress” is generally associated with
accepted.x: The name “Indian National Congress” is credited to Dadabhai Naoroji.
accepted.tq: Separate the person credited with the nomenclature from the founder-organiser and first president.
accepted.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. William Wedderburn — British founding member
2. Justice John Jardine — British founding member
3. A.O. Hume — General Secretary at the foundation
4. Dadabhai Naoroji — President of the first session
accepted.x: William Wedderburn and Justice John Jardine were British founding members, and Hume was General Secretary. Dadabhai Naoroji did not preside over the first session; W.C. Bonnerjee did.
accepted.tq: Use the founder-role swap trap to reject the statement assigning the first presidency to Naoroji.
accepted.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following sets contains only Andhra delegates to the first session of the Indian National Congress?
o: P. Anandacharlu, P. Rangaiah Naidu, Nyapathi Subbarao, Gutti Kesava Pillai and Venkata Subbarayudu
P. Anandacharlu, Dadabhai Naoroji, Nyapathi Subbarao, George Yule and Venkata Subbarayudu
P. Rangaiah Naidu, William Wedderburn, Gutti Kesava Pillai, Pherozeshah Mehta and Nyapathi Subbarao
Nyapathi Subbarao, W.C. Bonnerjee, P. Anandacharlu, Gutti Kesava Pillai and Dinshaw Wacha
accepted.x: The Andhra delegates listed were P. Anandacharlu, P. Rangaiah Naidu, Nyapathi Subbarao, Gutti Kesava Pillai and Venkata Subbarayudu.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure regional names and eliminate options containing national Congress presidents.
accepted.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about A.O. Hume is correct?
1. He was a retired member of the Indian Civil Service.
2. He was demoted in 1879 after a clash with Lord Lytton.
3. He retired in 1882 and settled in Shimla.
4. He drew the idea of local self-government from Lord Ripon.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four statements describe the background of A.O. Hume as given: his ICS career, clash and demotion under Lytton, retirement and settlement at Shimla, and influence of Ripon's local self-government policy.
accepted.tq: Verify each biographical detail separately before choosing the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A.O. Hume was considered closer politically to which group than to the Calcutta leaders?
accepted.x: Hume was regarded as closer to the Bombay-Poona groups than to the leaders of Calcutta.
accepted.tq: Test the regional political association of a person through a close geographical contrast.
accepted.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The second session of the Indian National Congress is associated with approximately how many delegates?
accepted.x: The second session at Calcutta in 1886 is cited with 436 delegates.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the sharply increased second-session attendance from the 72 delegates of 1885.
accepted.sec: INC sessions → president + venue (early sessions and FIRSTs)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: William Wedderburn presided over the 1889 session held at Bombay, not Calcutta. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Check the venue against the president and year, especially where adjacent sessions are involved.
accepted.sec: INC sessions → president + venue (early sessions and FIRSTs)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The 1890 session was held at Calcutta under Pherozeshah Mehta.
2. Kadambini Ganguly addressed the 1890 session.
3. Kadambini Ganguly was the first woman graduate of Calcutta University.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Pherozeshah Mehta presided at Calcutta in 1890, and Kadambini Ganguly addressed that session; she was the first woman graduate of Calcutta University.
accepted.tq: Combine the session detail with the biographical identity of the woman who addressed it.
accepted.sec: INC sessions → president + venue (early sessions and FIRSTs)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: P. Anandacharlu presided over the Nagpur session of 1891, the seventh session. Sayani presided in 1896, Dinshaw Wacha in 1901, and Naoroji in Lahore in 1893.
accepted.tq: Match the year, venue and president while using neighbouring sessions as distractors.
accepted.sec: INC sessions → president + venue (early sessions and FIRSTs)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: At which session of the Indian National Congress was “Vande Mataram” sung for the first time?
accepted.x: “Vande Mataram” was first sung at the Calcutta session of 1896, presided over by Rahimtulla M. Sayani; Rabindranath Tagore sang it.
accepted.tq: Link the cultural first with its exact session rather than the more famous inaugural sessions.
accepted.sec: INC sessions → president + venue (early sessions and FIRSTs)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who made the first appearance on the Indian National Congress platform at the 1901 Calcutta session?
accepted.x: Mahatma Gandhi made his first appearance on the Congress platform at the Calcutta session of 1901.
accepted.tq: Test the specific first appearance associated with a session instead of a later leadership role.
accepted.sec: INC sessions → president + venue (early sessions and FIRSTs)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who was the first Telugu woman to attend a session of the Indian National Congress?
accepted.x: Ponaka Kanakamma is identified as the first Telugu woman to attend an Indian National Congress session.
accepted.tq: Use the regional identity qualifier to distinguish this first from national-level women leaders.
accepted.sec: INC sessions → president + venue (early sessions and FIRSTs)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who was the youngest president of the Indian National Congress, according to the cited early Congress records?
accepted.x: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad became the youngest Congress president at the age of 35 at the special Delhi session of 1923.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the age-based “youngest” record from the later presidents associated with youth and radical politics.
accepted.sec: INC sessions → president + venue (early sessions and FIRSTs)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding Dadabhai Naoroji and W.C. Bonnerjee?
1. Dadabhai Naoroji — Calcutta 1886, Lahore 1893 and Calcutta 1906
2. W.C. Bonnerjee — Bombay 1885 and Allahabad 1892
3. Dadabhai Naoroji — two presidencies
4. W.C. Bonnerjee — three presidencies
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Naoroji presided three times—in Calcutta 1886, Lahore 1893 and Calcutta 1906—while Bonnerjee presided twice, at Bombay 1885 and Allahabad 1892.
accepted.tq: Use the presidency-count trap by checking both the locations and the number of terms.
accepted.sec: PERSON - Called as/Known as (Grand Old Man of India) and number of presidencies  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: W.C. Bonnerjee — Grand Old Man of India
accepted.x: Pherozeshah Mehta was known as the “Lion of Bombay.” Dadabhai Naoroji was the “Grand Old Man of India,” and Surendranath Banerjee was known as “Rashtraguru.”
accepted.tq: Discriminate among famous honorifics by pairing each title with its correct leader.
accepted.sec: PERSON - Called as/Known as (Grand Old Man of India) and number of presidencies  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs correctly represents the number of presidencies of the indicated leaders?
1. Surendranath Banerjee — 2
2. Rash Behari Ghosh — 2
3. Pherozeshah Mehta — 1
4. Dadabhai Naoroji — 2
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Surendranath Banerjee and Rash Behari Ghosh each presided twice, and Pherozeshah Mehta once. Dadabhai Naoroji presided three times, not twice.
accepted.tq: Check the numerical presidency counts and identify the single altered figure.
accepted.sec: PERSON - Called as/Known as (Grand Old Man of India) and number of presidencies  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Leader)
a. Surendranath Banerjee
b. Rash Behari Ghosh
c. Pherozeshah Mehta
List-II (Presidential sessions)
i. Calcutta 1890
ii. Poona 1895 and Ahmedabad 1902
iii. Surat 1907 and Madras 1908

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Surendranath Banerjee presided at Poona in 1895 and Ahmedabad in 1902; Rash Behari Ghosh at Surat in 1907 and Madras in 1908; Pherozeshah Mehta at Calcutta in 1890.
accepted.tq: Start from the unique single presidency of Pherozeshah Mehta and complete the code.
accepted.sec: PERSON - Called as/Known as (Grand Old Man of India) and number of presidencies  [APPSC]
